abstract: Mitochondria-ER contact sites (MERCs) play important roles in cellular functions such as lipid and Ca2+ transport and the regulation of mitochondrial dynamics. To better understand the functional diversity of MERCs, it is critical to identify proteins localized at these sites. Here, we employed CsFiND (Complementation assay using fusion of Split-GFP and TurboID) to identify MERC-associated proteins in HeLa cells. Proteomic and cell biological analyses identified ATAD1, a mitochondrial AAA-ATPase, as a MERC-associated protein. ATAD1 facilitates the transfer of GFP-Pex26{triangleup}C, a mislocalized peroxisomal membrane protein, from mitochondria to the ER. GFP-Pex26{triangleup}C is then degraded by the proteasome in a manner dependent on the ER-resident E3 ubiquitin ligase MARCH6. Notably, proteasome inhibition resulted in the accumulation of GFP-Pex26{triangleup}C at MERCs, suggesting that these sites may participate in this quality-control pathway. Together, these findings suggest a potential role for MERCs in the quality control of proteins mislocalized to mitochondria.
